subject: Franska 3
title: Subjunctive mood: an introduction to the subjonctif
sourceSummary: A first introduction to the present subjunctive (subjonctif) after expressions like il faut que, je veux que and je souhaite que.
topics: je veux que / je souhaite que

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Il faut que tu ___ (parler) plus lentement."
questions.opener: The present subjunctive of -er verbs is usually formed from the present-tense ils form minus -ent, plus the subjunctive ending.
questions.explanation: After "il faut que", the subjunctive is used. For "tu", the ending is -es: "que tu parles". The stem comes from "ils parlent" → parl-.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Il faut que nous ___ (finir) ce travail avant midi."
questions.opener: The nous and vous forms in the subjunctive often look the same as in the imperfect.
questions.explanation: The subjunctive for "nous" has the ending -ions: "que nous finissions". Compare with the present indicative "nous finissons" — only one letter differs, but the difference matters.

questions.topic: je veux que / je souhaite que
questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Je veux que tu ___ (venir) avec moi ce soir."
questions.opener: "Venir" is irregular in the subjunctive — the stem changes for je/tu/il/ils.
questions.explanation: "Venir" has the irregular subjunctive stem "vienn-" for je/tu/il/elle/ils: "que tu viennes". The ending -es, though, is the regular one for the tu form.

questions.topic: je veux que / je souhaite que
questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct when the subject is THE SAME in both clauses: "I want to leave tomorrow"?
questions.opener: When both clauses share the same subject, French uses the infinitive, not the subjunctive.
choices: Je veux que je parte demain.
Je veux que tu partes demain.
questions.explanation: When the subject of the main clause and the subordinate clause is the same, the infinitive is used: "je veux partir" (I want to leave). The subjunctive ("que je parte") is only used when the subjects differ, for example "je veux que TU partes".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Je souhaite que vous ___ (être) heureux."
questions.opener: "Être" has its own, entirely irregular subjunctive stem.
questions.explanation: "Être" in the subjunctive: que je sois, que tu sois, qu'il soit, que nous soyons, que vous soyez, qu'ils soient. For "vous" it becomes "soyez".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Il faut que tu ___ (avoir) de la patience."
questions.opener: "Avoir" also has an irregular subjunctive stem.
questions.explanation: "Avoir" in the subjunctive: que j'aie, que tu aies, qu'il ait, que nous ayons, que vous ayez, qu'ils aient. So "tu aies" is the correct form here.

questions.prompt: Explain which form fits each gap and why: "Mes parents veulent que je ___ (faire) mes devoirs avant de sortir, mais moi, je préfère ___ (sortir) d'abord et ___ (faire) mes devoirs après."
questions.opener: Compare the subjects in each clause: is it the same person who wants and who does, or different people?
steps: Gap 1: "mes parents veulent que JE fasse" — different subjects (the parents want, I do) → the subjunctive is required: "fasse" (irregular stem from faire).
Gap 2: "je préfère sortir" — same subject (I prefer, I go out) → infinitive: "sortir", not "que je sorte".
Gap 3: for the same reason, same subject again → infinitive: "faire", not the subjunctive.
The rule holds throughout: same subject in both parts → infinitive. Different subjects → subjunctive after expressions like vouloir que, falloir que, souhaiter que.

questions.prompt: How is the present subjunctive (subjonctif) formed and used after expressions like il faut que, je veux que and je souhaite que?
questions.opener: Formation, exceptions, and the important infinitive rule.
questions.answer: Formation (regular verbs): take the stem from the present-tense ils form (ils parlent → parl-) and add -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent: que je parle, que tu parles, qu'il parle, que nous parlions, que vous parliez, qu'ils parlent. Common irregular stems: être → sois/soyons/soyez, avoir → aie/ayons/ayez, faire → fasse, aller → aille/allions, pouvoir → puisse, savoir → sache. Used after expressions of will, necessity, or wish when the subjects DIFFER: il faut que, je veux que, je souhaite que, je voudrais que. Important rule: if the subject is the same in both clauses, the infinitive is used instead: "je veux partir" (not "que je parte").
